channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: The Human Experience · PhotoPlace Gallery
item.description: PhotoPlace Gallery's December call for photographs about the richness, complexity and diversity of human life. Portraits, street photography and documentary work are all welcome, as are pictures about current affairs, family, labour, culture, identity, community and the places we inhabit; the gallery asks for a broad reading of what it means to be human and will take work that is documentary or conceptual, quiet or dramatic, focused directly on people or on the places, events and traces of human presence that tell our stories. Juror Meredith Fleischer, founder of The MF Gallery in Royal Oak, Michigan and Director of The Detroit 15, will select up to 35 photographs for the Middlebury, Vermont gallery and roughly 40 more for the online gallery. All selected work is reproduced in the exhibition book, kept permanently on the PhotoPlace website and promoted through the gallery's publications and social channels; online-gallery selections receive the same catalog inclusion and promotion as the wall selections, and all selected artists are eligible for exhibition awards. Entries opened 7 September 2026 and close 5 October, with juror selections announced 19 October, prints due 20 November and the show running 4-26 December 2026, opening 4 December. There is no limit on the number of images submitted. The gallery's site-wide rules bar fully AI-generated images: all capture methods and photographic techniques are eligible, but submitted work must be created through photographic processes. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: $39 (5 images) + $6 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: 2027 Emerging Artist Prize · Cultural Council for Palm Beach County
item.description: A professional-development and recognition programme for visual artists in the early stages of their careers, run by the Cultural Council for Palm Beach County. Five emerging visual artists are selected, each receiving $3,500 in funding for the needs of their practice, four weeks of working studio space at the Norton Museum of Art between June and August 2027, one-to-one mentoring with an established professional in their field, visioning and strategic-planning coaching, group training on the business of an artistic practice, a professional headshot, and recognition in Council press materials and marketing. The programme is built around a cohort of peers at a similar career stage and runs from late January to September 2027. Applicants must live in Palm Beach County at the time of application, identify as an emerging visual artist early in a professional career, and be available for all scheduled in-person and virtual events. Applications open 11 September and close 23 October 2026; panelists meet the week of 16 November, recipients are notified the week of 14 December and announced on 14 January 2027 at the Kruger Family Gallery opening. The call does not enumerate accepted media, but the Council's artist-grant programme does support photographers: its 2026 Artist Innovation Fellows include Quinn Miller, whose funded project is a series of staged photographic compositions. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,500 + Studio residency.

item.title: Handmade · Site:Brooklyn Gallery
item.description: Site:Brooklyn's online juried exhibition on the intelligence of the human hand. The gallery is looking for work across all mediums that foregrounds the artist's hand as both process and subject - the point where thought becomes physical, direct and irreversible action - set against an era increasingly shaped by mechanical and digital reproduction. Juror Pallavi Surana is a New York-based arts writer and curator who has worked on projects with the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art and curator Cecilia Alemani, curated exhibitions at Smack Mellon, GHOSTMACHINE and the Hessel Museum of Art, and written for e-flux Criticism, ARTnews, The Art Newspaper and Ocula; she holds a graduate degree from the Center for Curatorial Studies at Bard College. The call is open to artists 18 and over working in all media, and entries must be original work measured in imperial dimensions. The exhibition runs online from 14 November to 14 December 2026. Entries close 26 October 2026 at 11:59pm MT. — Deadline: October 26, 2026. Fee: $26 (3 images) + $10 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Tombstone · Memento Mori Gallery & Tattoo
item.description: Memento Mori's annual Western-adjacent themed group show, timed to the Western Stock Show and, as always at this gallery, opening the door to the outsider, the lowbrow and the macabre. Memento Mori Gallery & Tattoo is a lowbrow/outsider contemporary art space at 6451 W. Colfax Ave in Lakewood, Colorado, in the 40West Arts District and on the First Friday art-walk circuit. Open nationally to 2D and 3D work; up to two pieces per artist at $25 each. Work must be for sale, with a 40% commission to the gallery, and must arrive physically ready to hang or display - hanging hardware already attached, wire preferred, no sawtooth hangers or adhesive mounts. Digital work is only shown if printed and framed or mounted properly. The gallery will not accept photographs of another artist's artwork, including street art, without the artist's express permission to show and sell the photograph. Out-of-state artists cover shipping both ways. Entries close 5 December 2026; drop-off 19 December, show 1-23 January 2027 with a First Friday reception on 1 January, 6-9pm, and pick-up 23 January. — Deadline: December 5, 2026. Fee: $25 per piece. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Members' Juried Exhibition · Tubac Center of the Arts
item.description: Tubac Center of the Arts opens its annual members' juried exhibition to artists across the United States, with all media accepted including video. Members may enter up to three 2D or 3D works completed in the last 24 months and not previously shown at TCA; giclee reproductions are not permitted. Entry is restricted to TCA members, but membership is bought directly from the art centre (Artist and Individual tiers are $50 a year) and is not itself juried - non-members are disqualified without refund, so join before applying. Juror Mary-Beth Buesgen is Lead Curator at the Mesa Contemporary Arts Museum and spent fifteen years at the ASU Art Museum as Curator and Collection Manager of its Ceramics Research Center. Awards total $900 - Best of Show $300, Award of Excellence $200, the Virginia Hall Contemporary Award $100, the Ursula Suess Abstract Award $100, an Award of Merit $100 and two Honorable Mentions at $50 - and are presented at the opening; the awards judge had not been appointed when the call was published and TCA says the prospectus will be updated once one is found. Best of Show also receives a solo exhibit in the Studio Gallery, 2 April - 16 May 2027. Entries open 21 September 2026 and the exhibition runs 8 January - 14 February 2027. All work must be for sale with a 40% commission, artists cover shipping both ways and must supply a prepaid return label. TCA's own timeline labels the 16 November deadline a Wednesday; 16 November 2026 is a Monday, and both the timeline and the CaFE portal give the same date. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: $35 (first entry) + $5 each additional; membership from $50/year. Prize: $900 in awards + Solo exhibition.

item.title: The Shape of Memory · Indiana University Kokomo
item.description: The IU Kokomo Art Gallery's juried summer exhibition asks artists to treat memory as the foundation of identity and expression rather than simple recollection, sharing their own stories through colour, light and distortion and translating how lived experience has shifted over time. Open to all artists over 18 who reside in the United States; work must be original, completed within the last two years, and works created by artificial intelligence are not eligible. Up to three works, 2D, 3D and video all eligible. The gallery cannot take payment through CaFE: after an entry is received, staff email an invoice from gallery2@iu.edu within roughly three to five business days, and the $25 fee must be paid before the entry is shown to the juror. Photographs and works on paper must arrive framed with a wire for hanging; the gallery walls take 2D pieces up to 9.5 feet tall and 9 feet wide through the doors, with two long walls that can carry pieces up to 25 feet. Accepted work is reproduced in an exhibition catalog. Entries close 2 April 2027, notifications 26 April, work received 18-21 May, exhibition 1 June - 7 July 2027 with a closing reception on 7 July, 4-6pm. The call names no juror. — Deadline: April 2, 2027. Fee: $25 (invoiced by email after entry). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Program Open Call 2028–2029 · NARS Foundation
item.description: The New York Art Residency and Studios (NARS) Foundation invites proposals for solo and group exhibitions in 2028 and 2029, for its Main Gallery on the fourth floor and the smaller Project Space on the second, both set among the artists' studios of an industrial building in Sunset Park, Brooklyn. NARS presents 12 to 13 exhibitions a year and reserves both spaces for early-career or underrepresented artists and curators chosen through this annual open call, which is open to new applicants and residency alumni alike. Artists, curators, collectives and cultural producers may propose shows of four to five weeks and are encouraged to activate the space with performances, artist talks and other events; selected applicants are invited to develop their proposals further with NARS providing space, support and resources, and a small honorarium is paid to the selected artist or curator at the end of the exhibition. The applicant - artist or curator - must be US-based, though a US-based curator may include international artists in a group proposal of three to five artists, and proposed artists must have confirmed their interest before the application is submitted. Applicants enrolled in a degree-granting art programme are not eligible, and anyone who has previously exhibited at NARS must wait two full years. One proposal per applicant per open call. NARS is a 501(c)(3) supported in part by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs; it cannot cover shipping, and artists should expect to install most of the work themselves. Applications ran 31 August to 21 September 2026, 11:59pm ET; decisions follow three to four weeks later. Materials: a resume, a 500-word proposal and up to ten work samples in image, text, audio or video. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition + Cash honorarium.

item.title: International Artist Residency 2027 — US-Based Fellowship · NARS Foundation
item.description: The NARS Foundation's International Artist Residency Program supports early- to mid-career artists working across all disciplines with three- and six-month residencies in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, alongside an international cohort. This is the autumn open call for US-based artists, covering 2027 Season I (January-March), Season II (April-June) and the two seasons together. Residents get a 24/7 studio of 250-300 square feet, three to four studio visits a month from curators, critics, art historians and gallerists, weekly A.S.A.P. gatherings, artist talks, panels, screenings and salons, and the season closes with a group exhibition in the NARS gallery and an open-studio event. NARS subsidises the cost for every selected US-based artist through a Partial Fellowship: for 2027 the fellowship is $7,292-$7,792 against a one-season programme fee of $9,962-$10,742, leaving the artist responsible for $2,950-$3,450, payable in full or in monthly instalments. One US-based artist per season also receives a Full Fellowship covering the entire programme fee, awarded by a jury of NARS staff and invited art professionals on artistic quality, level of need, studio practice and likely benefit from the NARS community; applicants must tick the relevant section of the form to be considered. The studio is a workspace only - housing, travel, materials and living costs are the artist's own, and there are no specialist facilities, though residents get access to Materials for the Arts. Photography is explicitly among the practices NARS expects, though it supplies no darkroom or equipment. Open to US-based visual artists with an active professional practice of at least three years, including international artists resident in the US for three years or more; students may apply if their programme ends before the residency starts. Applications ran 31 August to 21 September 2026, 11:59pm ET. Materials: a CV, a 400-word residency proposal, a 300-word bio and up to ten work samples. NARS is a 501(c)(3) supported in part by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Residency + Fellowship.

item.title: Singapore Documentary Festival 2027 — Photography Open Call · Objectifs — Centre for Photography and Film
item.description: The Singapore Documentary Festival, run by Objectifs, is looking for the best documentary photography from Southeast Asia for its 2027 edition. Six projects are selected for a group exhibition at the festival in April 2027; one receives the Truth Seeker Foundation Prize, a cash grant of S$5,000 for a project addressing critical social and environmental issues in the region, and the five runners-up each receive S$1,000. All six get budget return flights and accommodation to attend the opening and programmes in Singapore. Applicants must be from Southeast Asia (practitioners living outside the region may apply), have at least five years of professional photography experience including internships, editorial assignments and freelance work, be able to work in English and own full copyright in the submitted work; one project per applicant. Projects must be documentary and rooted in contemporary social issues in Southeast Asia; completed bodies of work must have concluded within the last five years, and ongoing projects are welcome. Every image must be made with a camera - AI-generated work is not accepted, and AI post-processing tools must not add or remove anything the camera captured. Submit a bio, portrait and CV, a synopsis of up to 250 words, 15 to 30 project images at 2000px on the longest side, and up to three recent projects. Deadline 30 September 2026, 2359hr Singapore time; shortlisted applicants may be contacted in October, selections announced in November, image selection and sequencing with the exhibition team from late November to January, production February-March 2027. The jury is Kelsang Dolma, Maye-E Wong, Amrita Chandradas and Chelsea Chua, alongside a representative of the Truth Seeker Foundation. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: S$5,000 + 5 × S$1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: The Song of Water — Sutri International Photography Festival 2026 · Museo di Palazzo Doebbing
item.description: The Doebbing Foto Festival's international open call selects the exhibition projects for the second Sutri International Photography Festival, running 21 November 2026 to 24 January 2027 in the hill town of Sutri, north of Rome. The 2026 theme is water, read through the title The Song of Water: the call asks photographers to treat water not as a backdrop but as the centre of a visual narrative - its vital force, the memory of territories, marine and river landscapes, climate change through drought, flood and coastal erosion, the human bond with water, architecture and water management, and the symbolism, spirituality, rites and myths of rebirth and purification. Open to individual photographers, professional and amateur, to photographic collectives and to photography schools, with no limit on age or nationality; every artistic approach from documentary to conceptual is accepted, and work made with AI is not. Each submission is a coherent project of 8 to 15 photographs, JPEG, at least 2500 pixels on the long side, with files named FirstName_LastName_WorkTitle_SequenceNumber; multiple distinct projects may be entered. Three winning projects are shown in full in the official festival circuit and promoted on the festival's website and social channels; other works judged worthy are placed in an off-circuit trail of 1 to 3 images per author in partner venues around the town. Printing and installation costs are covered in full by the organisers for every selected photographer, winners and off-circuit alike. The jury is the festival's artistic direction - Raffaella Canfarini, Vittorio Faggiani and Debora Valentini - with a final juror still to be named. Entries and proof of payment must arrive by 20 October 2026, 11:59pm, emailed to info@doebbingfotofestival.it with a title, captions, a short bio, a project text and the entry form from the site; the fee is paid by bank transfer. — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: €20 (first project) + €15 second + €10 each additional. Prize: Festival exhibition.

item.title: Schoenfeld-Capa Scholarship for Concerned Photography · International Center of Photography
item.description: A full-tuition scholarship created in honour of ICP founder Cornell Capa's idea of Concerned Photography - a practice rooted in empathy, ethical storytelling and social engagement - and of longtime ICP board member Pat Schoenfeld. The award covers the entire $12,500 tuition for ICP's online One-Year Certificate in Documentary Practice: Visual Storytelling, and is open to all domestic and international applicants. Recipients are chosen by ICP's Scholarship Committee on the strength of the application and portfolio, with emphasis on clarity of vision and potential impact in documentary photography. Both the programme application and the scholarship form must be submitted by the 18 October 2026 deadline; the programme application itself carries a $60 fee, so a scholarship recipient's total cost is that fee alone. Scholarships and fellowships cannot be combined - an applicant may receive only one award - and applicants are automatically considered for ICP's merit-based awards through a section inside the programme application. Scholarships are only available to students enrolling in the One-Year Certificate programmes; part-time courses and Open Education workshops are not eligible. ICP is not an accredited institution, so the certificate does not qualify for federal student loans. Applications are made through SlideRoom; results are emailed with the admission decision. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: $12,500 full tuition scholarship.

item.title: MurthyNAYAK Foundation Scholarship · International Center of Photography
item.description: Offered by ICP with support from PhotoSouthAsia, the MurthyNAYAK Foundation Scholarship is a $10,000 tuition award for artists from the South Asia region who show exceptional achievement and potential in photography. Three scholarships are given, each covering $10,000 of the $12,500 tuition for one of ICP's online One-Year Certificate programmes: Curatorial Practice in Photography, Writing and the Photographic Image, or Documentary Practice: Visual Storytelling. Eligibility is limited to applicants from and currently residing in South Asia - Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka - who demonstrate strong artistic ability, engagement with contemporary photographic practice and a commitment to impactful projects. Selection is based on the same portfolio, curatorial project proposal or writing sample required for the programme application, and both the programme application and the scholarship form must be in by 18 October 2026. The programme application carries a $60 fee. Scholarships cannot be combined, so an applicant may hold only one award, and the scholarships are open only to students enrolling in the One-Year Certificate programmes rather than part-time courses or Open Education workshops. Applications are made through SlideRoom. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: 3 × $10,000 tuition scholarship.

item.title: The Power of Blue · MVA Gallery
item.description: National call for work built around the colour blue at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. The gallery invites artists, photographers and sculptors at every level to answer a set of questions about how blue functions in their work: whether it permeates the whole image or sits in small sections, whether it appears in objects, in nature or in abstract design, and whether it is decorative or structural. Blue is framed as a contradictory colour, standing for freedom, imagination, trust and faith on one side and coldness, loneliness and sadness on the other. There is no restriction on subject matter or style, traditional and non-traditional approaches are equally welcome, and all photographic processes are accepted; there is no cutoff date for when the work was made. Open to US residents aged 18 and over. Entry is $35 for three images and $5 for each additional image up to nine. Jurying is by an anonymous rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers and academics. Awards are an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery second room, an optional $200 Director Choice award, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from everyone shown at the gallery during the year. Work must be wired for hanging, no larger than 48 inches framed and under 50 lbs; photographs should be framed in black or white with white or off-white mats if presented traditionally, and plexiglass is preferred over glass for shipped pieces. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs 28 February to 26 March 2027. — Deadline: September 29, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Creating Collages · MVA Gallery
item.description: National call for collage and collage-like work at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, with photomontage and digital collage named explicitly alongside mixed media, assemblage and decoupage. The gallery is interested in the juxtaposition of painted and photographic imagery with coloured paper, printed text, fabric and found objects, and in work that is two-dimensional or three-dimensional, structured or floating, serious, humorous, irreverent or satirical. Any subject matter is welcome. Artists, photographers, printmakers and sculptors at every level may enter and all photographic processes are accepted; there is no cutoff date for when the work was made. Open to US residents aged 18 and over. Entry is $35 for three images and $5 for each additional image up to nine. Jurying is by an anonymous rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers and academics. Awards are an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery second room, an optional $200 Director Choice award, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from everyone shown at the gallery during the year. Work must be wired for hanging, no larger than 48 inches framed and under 45 lbs; photographs should be framed in black or white with white or off-white mats if presented traditionally, and plexiglass is preferred over glass for shipped pieces. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs 28 February to 26 March 2027. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Artist in Residence · Great Basin National Park
item.description: Free open call for three 2027 artist residencies at Great Basin National Park in eastern Nevada, run with the Great Basin National Park Foundation, which funds the programme. Artists are surrounded by the park from the 13,063-foot summit of Wheeler Peak to the depths of Lehman Caves, with wilderness solitude and renowned dark-sky stargazing. Applicants choose the seasons they want to be considered for: a winter residency of two to three weeks in January or February with park housing (a furnished private bedroom in a shared living space with kitchen, bathroom and laundry), a summer residency of two to three weeks in July or August that is a camping residency with gear supplied by the Foundation, or a fall residency of two to three weeks in September or October, which can be timed to overlap the park Astronomy Festival. The two surfaces disagree about the fall term: the park's own page lists it as a housed residency on the same terms as winter, and notes that fall and winter residencies with NPS housing require a background check, while the CaFÉ prospectus calls it a camping-only residence — confirm with the coordinator before choosing that season. The park is remote: the nearest town, Baker, has few or no amenities and Ely is 60 to 70 miles away; cell service is limited and campgrounds have no internet or electricity. Open to visual artists, literary artists, musicians and other creative media artists residing anywhere, with one of the three places held for a regional artist living and working in Nevada or Utah. Each resident becomes an NPS volunteer, presents one public programme in the park, delivers a virtual programme within six months and a digital portfolio within three months, and donates one physical piece plus a digital representation to the Foundation within a year under a deed of gift, which may be displayed in the park for up to three years. The digital portfolio will not be monetised and exclusive rights are not requested; artists are always credited. Applications are reviewed by jury panels of past participants, subject-matter experts, local community members and park staff, and selected artists are announced by press release in January. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 2-3 week residency with park lodging or campsite.

item.title: Florida’s Natural Beauty 2026 · Audubon of Martin County
item.description: Juried photography contest and exhibition presented by Audubon of Martin County and hosted by the Historical Society of Martin County at the Elliott Museum in Stuart, Florida. Open to all amateur and professional photographers residing in the US; every photograph and video must have been taken in Florida. Six categories: Birds, Wildlife, Flora/Landscape, Creative, Video and Cell Phone Photography. Up to seven images or videos may be entered per category, each image in one category only, at $25 per uploaded photograph for non-members and $20 for Audubon of Martin County members. Only global adjustments are allowed outside the Creative category, and the use of AI is not permitted in the Creative category. Camera-trap images are disqualified, recognisable individuals need a signed release, and photographs previously entered into an Audubon of Martin County contest are not eligible. Awards are Best in Show $300, and in each category first $200, second $100 and third $50, with honourable mentions at the judges discretion; judging is blind, by a panel of three independent photography experts. This is not a digital-only exhibit: accepted images must be supplied as museum-quality framed, canvas, acrylic or metal prints, minimum 8 inches on the short side and no more than 20 by 24 inches including the frame, wired for hanging. Notification 11 December 2026; opening reception and awards at the Elliott Museum 21 January 2027; exhibition on view daily 22 January to 25 February 2027. Photographers keep copyright, with limited permission granted for archival, publicity and promotional use. Sales are split 75% to the artist and 25% to the Museum. Out-of-area entrants may ship accepted prints prepaid round trip. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: $25 per photo (non-members) / $20 members. Prize: $300 Best in Show + museum exhibition.

item.title: Luis Ferreira Alves Photography Award 2026
item.description: Second edition of the biennial Luis Ferreira Alves International Photography Competition — A Contemporary Look at Architecture, a free award founded in tribute to the Portuguese architectural photographer and run from Porto by Cityscopio with Porto City Council, the Faculty of Architecture of the University of Porto and Casa da Arquitectura. Open to photographers of all nationalities, working individually or collectively, with a series of 9 to 11 images engaging a single work of architecture, a group of works or a broader architectural context; analogue or digital, colour or black and white, plus a project statement of up to 2,000 characters. First prize is EUR 10,000, second EUR 4,000 and third a EUR 1,500 photographic-equipment voucher; the 2026 edition adds a Portuguese Emerging Photography Award (a further EUR 1,500 voucher) for Portuguese artists. Up to ten finalists, plus any special mentions, are shown in the official exhibition and published in the catalogue, and judging is blind through the platform. Generative AI is not permitted. Submissions open 25 September 2026 and close 1 January 2027 at 23:59 mainland Portugal time; the first international edition drew 1,495 entries from 99 countries. — Deadline: January 1, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: €10,000 / €4,000 / €1,500 voucher + Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: Framed: Shadow and Light · Black Box Gallery
item.description: Juried group photography show at Black Box Gallery in Portland on shadow and light — dramatic shadows and patterns in black and white, ethereal and moody shadow and texture in colour, and the range of ways contemporary photographers read the two together. Juror Todd Johnson, the gallery's founder and director, selects 26 photographs for the gallery walls and a further 50 for the online gallery annex; all 76 appear in a catalogue published through Blurb. The gallery prints, mats and frames every exhibited work at no cost to the photographer, using an Epson archival inkjet setup and its own 18 × 24 inch frames, and keeps exhibition prints in its flat files for two years to show to collectors and curators. Artists retain all rights to the file and the print, no print is sold without the photographer's prior consent and a signed authentication document, and work does not have to be offered for sale; if it is, the split is 50/50. Entry is $40 for up to five photographs, submitted by email after paying through PayPal. Open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional. Exhibition runs November 1–25, 2026. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Gallery exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Pride Photo 2027
item.description: Free annual international contest from the Amsterdam non-profit Pride Photo, open to photographers worldwide of all ages, backgrounds and levels, for work that explores LGBTQIA+ lives, identities and visual languages. Two categories: STORIES, a project series of 3 to 15 images, and SINGLE IMAGES, up to five standalone works; two projects per application and multiple applications allowed. Documentary photography, portraiture, collage and photographic intervention are all welcome. Selected photographers receive EUR 500 for each work included in the Pride Photo Exhibition 2027, which opens publicly in Amsterdam and then travels nationally and internationally from spring 2027 to spring 2028, with credited features across Pride Photo's print and digital platforms. The 2027 jury is chaired by Supranav Dash with Katy Hundertmark, Papa De, Marit Lena Hermmann and Marwan Kaboor. Any use of AI must be declared and explained, and images created entirely through generative AI are not accepted; Pride Photo's published reasoning is that images representing LGBTQIA+ lives should be grounded in lived reality. Copyright stays with the photographer. Submissions close 31 October 2026 at 23:59 CET; winners are announced in June 2027. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500 per selected work + Exhibition.

item.title: Carroll Harris Simms National Black Art Competition and Exhibition · African American Museum, Dallas
item.description: Biennial national competition and exhibition at the African American Museum in Dallas, open to Black artists residing in the United States. The museum began the competition in 1976 to build its collection and give Black artists a venue, and named it in 1999 for Carroll Harris Simms, co-founder of the Texas Southern University art department. A $1,000 award goes to one artist in each of six categories — painting, sculpture, mixed media, drawing, printmaking and photography — and one of the six category winners is chosen Best in Show, which carries a solo exhibition at the museum within the following two years; the Best in Show artist agrees to donate a work from that show to the museum's permanent collection. Entry is $25, with one to four images per work in JPEG at 300 dpi and a maximum 5 MB per file, plus an artist statement and current biography; sculpture entries take one to four views. Up to three separate applications are allowed. AI-generated art and photography are not accepted. Entry deadline November 20, 2026, with selection notifications November 23–27 and accepted work delivered by January 17, 2027. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $1,000 per category + Solo exhibition.

item.title: 43rd Five State Photography Competition & Exhibition · Hays Arts Council
item.description: Annual regional fine-art photography competition run by the Hays Arts Council in Kansas and open to photographers living in Kansas, Nebraska, Missouri, Oklahoma and Colorado. Now in its 43rd year, the exhibition is the anchor of the Winter Art Walk and opens to the public each December. Any photographic process and any subject is eligible, provided the work was made in the last three years and has not been in a previous Five State exhibition; each photograph is entered and judged in one of three categories — Nature, People or Open. Juror Elise Kirk, Associate Professor of Photography and chair of the Department of Visual Art at the University of Kansas, selects 100 photographs for exhibition and awards $1,500 in cash across the three categories. Entry is $25 for the first two photographs and $7.50 for each of up to two more, paid by card or by cheque. Files are JPEG only, no larger than 30 MB, at least 1,200 pixels on the long side, in a 4:5 aspect ratio, and selected work is printed by the photographer at 8 × 10 inches; the council mats and frames every accepted print itself. Entries and payments are due October 23, 2026, acceptances go out by November 4, and the exhibition runs December 5, 2026 to January 31, 2027. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: $25 (2 photos) + $7.50 each additional. Prize: $1,500 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Companions · L.A. Photo Curator
item.description: Open call from L.A. Photo Curator on the animals we live alongside — the pets that greet us, wait for us and quietly become companions rather than animals we care for. Juried by Laurie Freitag, who founded L.A. Photo Curator eleven years ago. Every entrant is included in the online group exhibition with an artist statement, biography and website link, and the first-place photographer receives a solo online exhibition, an online article with a Q&A drawing on the juror's responses, and their image on the L.A. Photo Curator splash page for a month; selected work is also considered for the platform's Top 40 Images of the Year and its Photographer of the Year. One participating photographer is invited to serve as guest juror alongside Freitag on a future call. Entry is $25 for either three or six images, paid through PayPal and then emailed as a ZIP of JPEGs at 1024 pixels on the long side. Five per cent of entry fees goes to a charity chosen by the winner. Open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional. Deadline September 27, 2026. — Deadline: September 27, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Solo online exhibition.

item.title: The Chico Review 2027 · Charcoal Book Club
item.description: Juried application to the eleventh Chico Review, the photobook retreat organised by Charcoal Book Club at Chico Hot Springs Resort in Paradise Valley, Montana, March 15–21, 2027. Eighty photographers are selected by jury from open application and spend seven days with more than twenty-five photographers, bookmakers, gallerists, curators and photobook publishers; each attendee receives ten 20-minute portfolio reviews plus artist lectures, panel discussions, peer reviews and evening programming. One attending photographer is awarded the Charcoal Publishing Prize, and their project is published and distributed worldwide by Charcoal Book Club. Six merit scholarships are awarded on the strength of the submitted work — one full tuition ($5,450), two half tuition ($2,675) and three partial ($1,500) — with academic discounts and limited need-based scholarships also available on acceptance. Applicants submit a cohesive body of work; there is no theme. 2027 speakers include Paul Graham, Barbara Bosworth, Daniel Arnold, Rena Effendi, JH Engström, Paul D'Amato, Emma Hardy and Hannah Modigh. Application fee $25 for Charcoal Book Club members, $50 otherwise, rising to a $65 late entry fee in late November. Attendance, if selected, is $5,450 tuition and board plus lodging at $70–$250 a night. — Deadline: November 29, 2026. Fee: $50 non-members / $25 members / $65 late entry after Nov 23. Prize: Book publication + 6 merit scholarships ($5,450 / $2,675 / $1,500).

item.title: Daisy Lane: Print & Book Artist Residency 2027 · Bainbridge Island Museum of Art
item.description: Free-to-apply residency at Daisy Lane, the Bainbridge Island Museum of Art's new print and book arts studio minutes from the museum, for artists working in book arts, letterpress, screenprinting, Risograph and related print forms — which includes photographers making artists' books and photobooks. Two residents are in place at any time, one local and one travelling, each for two to four weeks, with studio access from 8am to 10pm daily and easy access to the museum, its events and the Cynthia Sears Artists' Books Collection. The studio was equipped in part with presses and equipment acquired from Paper Hammer and Marquand Books, the letterpress, printmaking and book design studio in Tieton, Washington. Selection is on conceptual creativity, technical knowledge and familiarity with at least one of the studio's processes; familiarity need not be advanced, and orientation and instruction on the equipment are provided. Applicants submit contact information, a project proposal, an artist biography and five to ten work samples. Applications for 2027 residents open October 1, 2026 and close December 1, 2026. There is no application fee; CaFÉ offers an optional $25 support payment. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free (optional $25 support fee). Prize: Residency (2–4 weeks).

item.title: Long River Review 2027 — Art & Photography
item.description: Free open submissions for the art and photography section of Long River Review, the University of Connecticut's literary and arts magazine, now on its twenty-ninth print issue and run by an MFA-student editorial board. The magazine welcomes all art mediums including photography, illustration, printmaking, painting, comics, drawing and mixed media; the submission limit is five to ten pieces with a 150-word artist statement explaining the work. Files should be TIFF or EPS at 350 dpi, 5.75 inches minimum to 8 inches maximum width, in CMYK for colour and greyscale for black and white. Only unpublished work is accepted; simultaneous submissions are fine if you notify the editors. Accepted contributors give first North American serial rights, after which rights revert, and receive two copies of the issue their work appears in; the magazine is not in a position to pay contributors. Art submitted by UConn students is additionally considered for the Gloriana Gill Art Awards and the Long River Art Award. AI-generated visual content is not published and the editors describe the review process they follow if a submission is suspected. Reading period September 15 to December 15, with decisions by the end of April. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: The Fine Odd · Hand Fetish Projects
item.description: Rolling open call for The Fine Odd, a fine-art artbook from independent arthouse Hand-Fetish-Projects, published in two separate volumes — 01 Photography and 02 Visual Art & Print-Based Work. The photography volume is open to conceptual, documentary, staged, experimental, analogue, digital, fashion and manipulated work, submitted as a single image or as part of a series. There is no fixed theme: artists respond to “odd” as a condition rather than a subject, and 18+ themes, sexuality and fetish are welcome but not required. Selected artists receive two dedicated spreads, 2–5 works, bespoke layout with full credits, permanent archiving, a complimentary digital copy and discounted print copies. Artists retain full copyright; HFP takes a non-exclusive licence that also covers derivative retail products such as prints and postcard sets, with revenue split 55% to the artist on single-artist items. $15 for three pieces, $25 for five. No deadline is published — submissions are reviewed on a rolling basis. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: $15–$25. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: LIGHT · California Art League
item.description: A live juried exhibition on the theme of Light, presented by the California Art League at bG Gallery in Bergamot Station, Santa Monica, and hung there from 3 to 18 November 2026. Om Navon Bleicher, who founded bG Gallery in 2009 and directs it, is the sole juror and picks both the show and the awards from the digital images submitted. Awards are $800 Best of Show, $500 first place, $200 second place, $100 third place, three honourable mentions and the Theodore Herman Award for Photography. The League - founded in 1948 as the Valley Artists Guild by the sculptor Henry Van Wolf and renamed in 2012 - says painters, sculptors, photographers and collage artists are welcome, and this call accepts drawing, painting, photographs, digital art, mixed media, collage and sculpture; no performance art or AI is accepted. Work must be original and created by the artist from conception to completion, and must not have been shown in a CAL exhibit before. The call is open to CAL members and non-members alike: one or two entries cost $35 for members with dues current and $55 for non-members, the $20 difference being a one-time charge that also gives the new artist a discounted CAL membership; further works are $5 each up to a total of six. There is a 30-inch maximum frame width for wall art. Entries close 11 October at midnight PST and artists are notified on 19 October. Accepted work must be hand delivered to the gallery on 2 November; all work must be for sale and must not be offered for sale anywhere else until 30 days after the show closes, with bG Gallery taking a 50% commission on sales in that period. The opening reception and awards presentation is on Saturday 7 November, with an artists' talk on 15 November and pick-up on 19 November. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $55 non-members / $35 members for 1-2 works, $5 each additional (max 6). Prize: $800 Best of Show + $500/$200/$100 places + Exhibition.

item.title: Palette in Play: How Artists Use Color · Belvedere Tiburon Library
item.description: Juried group exhibition at THE Gallery, the exhibition space of the Belvedere Tiburon Library in Tiburon, California, asking Bay Area artists for the work that best exemplifies how they use colour. The gallery wants submissions that help it “unpack and decode your color choices” — does your use of colour capture feeling, does it manipulate mood, or is your love of colour self-evident? Glowing, vibrant work that shapes perception and muted, calm choices that still the viewer's mind are equally welcome. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, fine art prints, mixed media and textile/fabric art. The show is two-dimensional only, including low-relief work up to five inches deep; sculpture, suspended work and reproductions of your own art in another medium (an offset lithograph of your painting, a giclée of your watercolour) are not considered, and art created using artificial intelligence will not be considered. The library is a family destination and the gallery asks that subject matter suit that audience. THE Gallery blind-juries most of its exhibitions and asks that artist statements omit the artist's name. Selected work hangs 19 November 2026 to 13 January 2027, with an opening reception on 19 November, and is seen by the several thousand visitors who attend gallery and library events or stroll through the library. Entry is $35 for up to three submissions, each of which may carry two additional detail images. All work must be for sale, with 70% to the artist and 30% to THE Gallery; pieces must be ready to hang, between 8 x 10 inches and 72 x 60 inches, and under 50 pounds. Drop-off and pick-up are in person in Tiburon. The prospectus names no cash award — selection into the show is the outcome. — Deadline: October 3, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Flow State · The Aplomb Project
item.description: Juried group exhibition at Aplomb Contemporary Gallery in Dover, New Hampshire, built around Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi's description of flow as “a state in which people are so involved in an activity that nothing else seems to matter”. The gallery is seeking work made in that state of creativity and, in alignment with the mission of its parent non-profit, invites submissions reflecting healing, resilience, identity, transformation, grief, hope, strength or personal perspective. “All interpretations and mediums are welcome”, and the gallery's own calls page names photography alongside painting, drawing, sculpture and mixed media. The juror is Marisa Companion, an artist and educator with an MFA from California Institute of the Arts whose work has been featured at the Danforth Museum of Art in Framingham and at Art Basel Miami. Artists may submit one to six works and may apply from any geographic location. Two-dimensional work must arrive securely ready to hang, either framed or gallery-wrapped with painted sides; three-dimensional work in all mediums and multimedia work are also considered. The show runs 6 November to 15 December 2026 with an opening reception on 6 November, and accepted work is due by 3 November. Entry is $35 and the organisers will waive it for artists for whom the fee is a barrier — contact them before applying. Artists retain 60% of sales; The Aplomb Project, a 501(c)(3) that uses art to support people affected by trauma, illness and life transitions, retains a 40% commission and absorbs transaction processing fees. Selected artists ship or deliver their own work, and shipped work must include a prepaid return label or be collected in person. The prospectus names no cash award. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Gomma Photography Grant 2026
item.description: The Gomma Grant returns for its thirteenth edition, run by Gomma Publishing Ltd - the imprint behind Gomma Magazine, publishing since 2004 and, on its own account, having worked with Roger Ballen, Anders Petersen, Michael Ackerman, Momo Okabe, Keizo Kitajima, Araki and Daido Moriyama. The organisers say they look for photographers who develop their own language instead of following trends, and that they judge the work rather than the CV, reputation or number of followers. Entries are welcome across documentary, portrait, landscape, conceptual, black and white, colour, analogue and digital, from a project that may be unfinished, ongoing or completed, and it does not matter how long ago the work was begun. Each entry is 8 to 24 images at 72 dpi, minimum 1,500 pixels on the long edge, with a short description plus an optional artist statement and biography. Multiple entries are allowed provided they come from different bodies of work, and two photographers may submit a collaborative project jointly. The fee depends on which deadline you make: €19 by Friday 25 September, €25 by Thursday 15 October and €35 by the final deadline on Thursday 5 November, with the submission clock set to Hawaii Standard Time (UTC-10). Seven awards are listed. First Prize takes €1,000 and a potential publishing deal with Gomma Publishing and its network; the Gomma New Flavour award takes €300 and the same publishing offer; Second Prize €200 and Third Prize €100; the Honorable Mention, Best Documentary Award and Best Black and White Award carry no cash. Every award adds promotion through Gomma's own channels and media partners, and the organisers say winning work is put to international galleries and curators. AI-generated images are not accepted. No jury is published for this edition - the only answer the FAQ gives on the subject is scoped to 2025, which it says was judged in secret. One conflict worth knowing before you plan around it: the guidelines block says winners are announced in Spring 2027 while the Deadline & Fees block on the same page says February 2027, and the entry form sides with Spring 2027. — Deadline: November 5, 2026. Fee: €19 early bird to Sep 25, €25 to Oct 15, then €35. Prize: €1,000 + €300 + €200 + €100 + possible publication.

item.title: Annual Art For All 2027 · Art Center Waco
item.description: Art Center Waco, a Texas arts centre running since 1973, opens its second Annual Art for All juried exhibition to emerging and established visual artists living in the state of Texas and aged 18 or over. The framing is deliberately wide - the centre's mission is that art is for everyone - and all 2D and 3D media are eligible, with sculpture, painting, drawing, printmaking, photography, mixed media and ceramic fine art named in the prospectus. Read the media rule to its end before ruling yourself out: it says "no digital prints", but the same paragraph clarifies that what is barred is reproductions of original works, giving giclee prints of paintings as the example, "while photographic prints are allowed", and a later hanging clause confirms it by requiring works on paper, photography and collage on paper to be framed and ready to hang. Up to three pieces may be entered for $25, each made within the past five years and not previously shown at Art Center Waco. There is no minimum size and a 72-inch maximum in any direction, with wall works capped at 60lbs; sawtooth hangers, clip frames, keyhole slots, loose eye hooks, adhesives, velcro and command strips are all refused. Three awards go to work in the show - $500 Best of Show, $300 second and $200 third - chosen from the hung exhibition and announced at the opening reception. Selected artists are notified on or before Friday 13 November 2026 and must get their work to the gallery between 1 and 18 December, by drop-off or shipping; shipped work carries a $15 handling fee per box or crate, billed separately after acceptance. Everything hangs in the Beard Gallery at 701 S. 8th Street from 7 January to 5 March 2027, priced for sale with a 30% commission to the centre and 70% to the artist, and the centre says proceeds from sales support both the participating artists and its own exhibitions, education and community programmes. No juror is named for this edition. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: $25 (+$15 per shipped box if accepted). Prize: $500 Best of Show + $300 + $200 + Exhibition.

item.title: 19th Annual Open Juried Photographic Exhibit · Cary Photographic Artists
item.description: Cary Photographic Artists, founded in 2007 and described on its own site as the Triangle's only group whose mission is to develop and enhance the practice of photographic art, has run this open juried show every autumn since then. It is a print show: digital files go through CaFE but are not what is judged, and every entry must be printed, mounted, framed and hand-delivered to the Cary Senior Center on Monday 19 October before it is judged - the club's homepage tells photographers who cannot get work to Cary, NC not to enter. About 200 images are typically submitted and 50 are hung. There are two categories, MONOCHROME and COLOR, each with $200, $125 and $75 places and three honourable mentions, plus the Bobbi Hopp Best in Show Award of $400, named for the club's late founder. Any photographic process may be used as long as the photographic process is dominant; canvas wraps and prints on wood, metal, foam core or other surfaces are accepted; framed size cannot exceed 33 inches on the longest edge; work accepted into a prior CPA juried or digital exhibition is not eligible; and the artist's signature must not be visible on the front during judging. No AI or text-to-generative-fill images are accepted, and entrants retain the rights to their images. The jurors are Sarah Shea Roberto, a North Carolina photographer specialising in the silver gelatin darkroom who teaches experimental darkroom techniques at the NC State University Crafts Center, and Stacy Bloom Rexrode, Curator of Exhibitions and Collections with the City of Raleigh. Entry opens on CaFE on 15 September; artists whose images are accepted are telephoned on the evening of 20 October and work that is not selected is collected the next day; the show hangs at the Cary Senior Center from 20 October to 19 December; and a reception with comments by the jurors and presentation of awards is at 6pm on Friday 23 October. — Deadline: October 16, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 3 images). Prize: $400 Best in Show + $200/$125/$75 per category.

item.title: World Sports Photography Awards 2027
item.description: The World Sports Photography Awards, sponsored by Canon, are open for their 2027 edition, free of charge and open to photographers of all ages from any country - the organisers expect mainly professional and semi-professional sports photographers, with some amateurs. Entrants may submit up to ten single images made between December 2025 and November 2026, placed across 24 sporting categories, with no limit on how many categories one photographer enters. Each category produces a top ten - Gold, Silver, Bronze and seven Special Merits - and an overall top three is chosen from the category Gold winners. The organisers say prizes are provided by the awards' sponsors but publish no schedule of them, and this cycle is run entirely online with no in-person awards. Judging is by a panel of ninety named senior figures from sport, media, brands and photography, recused from any category where they have a conflict of interest; they include Tony Duffy, the photographer who founded Allsport, Lee Martin of Getty Images, Justin Feck of The Daily Mail, Andrés Ballesteros of the EFE agency and Jamie Schwaberow of NCAA Photos. The manipulation rules are strict and worth reading before entering: no multiple exposures, polyptychs or stitched panoramas made in software (in-camera versions are accepted), no adding, rearranging, reversing, distorting or removing anything within the frame, cropping and the removal of sensor dust or scan scratches only, and no staging or recreation of events without disclosure in the caption. All entries must be created with a camera; synthetic or AI-generated images are barred and generative fill brings automatic disqualification. Entrants keep copyright and grant a non-exclusive, irrevocable licence for uses connected with the awards, with no payment due for them. Entries opened on 9 September 2026, a shortlist follows in December and the winners are announced on 14 January 2027. — Deadline: November 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Beyond the Mountains Fund 2026–27 · Tinworks Art
item.description: Beyond the Mountains Fund is Montana's arm of the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts' Regional Regranting Program, run by Tinworks Art, a non-profit arts organisation in Bozeman; the fund joined the network as a regional partner in 2026. Each year the fund awards one grant of $10,000 and ten grants of $5,000 to Montana-based artists for independent, public-facing projects that encourage experimentation and collaboration, with priority given to Indigenous, emerging and mid-career artists; established artists are eligible when seeking support to explore new, experimental or previously underdeveloped areas of their practice. Projects must take place in Montana, be artist-organised and self-initiated, and operate within a visual arts context the fund defines broadly to include visual art, performance art, digital art and mixed media. They must happen outside a conventional studio or commercial gallery setting, be accessible to the public in community spaces, and charge no admission or participation fee; 501(c)(3) organisations and for-profit businesses cannot apply. One proposal per person per cycle, and past awardees may reapply two years after their award date. The application asks for contact details, an artist bio, a 250-character project summary, a 3,000-character project description and a basic budget, plus information on collaborators, the intended audience or site and any outreach plans; supplementary imagery and sketches are welcome, and timeline and budget templates are provided. Applications are reviewed by a panel of three to five compensated artists and arts professionals with strong ties to the local and regional arts community and expertise in nontraditional, community-centred art practices. Half the award is disbursed up front and half on completion of an interim project report. The 2026 window opened August 1 and closes October 1, 2026 at 11:59pm MT; grantees are announced in December 2026, initial project activities run 1 January to 30 June 2027, an interim report is due 30 June 2027, project activities complete over July–November 2027 and final reports and documentation are due 31 December 2027. Free to apply, through Submittable. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000–$10,000.

item.title: Provision Fund 2026 · Real Art Ways
item.description: The Provision Fund is Connecticut's Andy Warhol Foundation Regional Regranting programme, administered by Real Art Ways in Hartford and running for the first time in 2026. Six $10,000 grants are awarded through a juried open call to artists based in Connecticut, and there is no fee to apply. Projects must be grounded in the visual arts - which the fund defines as broadly as possible, with other disciplines allowed so long as visual art is the driving force - and must have a public-facing component; the guidelines offer publications, living room galleries, garage performance spaces, virtual reality film screenings, community gardens, and oral history and archival projects as examples of what that might look like. Individual artists, artist groups and informal collectives are all eligible and encouraged; applicants must be independent and unincorporated, non-profit organisations cannot apply, work commissioned by museums or universities is ineligible, and funded projects will not take place at Real Art Ways. The lead applicant must live in Connecticut, may not be a full-time student and needs a Social Security number for 1099 reporting, while collaborators may live anywhere. A competitive application must include a line item paying the artists for their labour, and the artists must retain creative and financial control. The application asks for a project title, a 150-word summary, a 500-word narrative, a timeline, a location description of up to 250 words, a budget, five to ten work samples (still images plus up to five video links) and a CV. Three guest jurors - Saya Woolfalk, Seph Rodney and Kelsey Halliday Johnson - assess artistic excellence and clarity of vision, feasibility, the quality of the public-facing component and thoughtful engagement with community, site or social context. Applications opened July 20 and close September 20, 2026 at 11:59pm; awardees are announced in November 2026 and the grant period runs January 15, 2027 to January 15, 2028. Submissions go through Submittable. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000.

item.title: Precipice Fund Round 15 · Portland Institute for Contemporary Art
item.description: Since 2013 the Precipice Fund has supported unincorporated visual art collectives, alternative spaces, artist-run initiatives and collaborative projects in and around Portland, Oregon. It is administered by the Portland Institute for Contemporary Art as part of the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts' Regional Regranting Program, and from Round 15 additional support from The Ford Family Foundation extends its capacity to invest in artist-run spaces and independent exhibition projects. Round 15 awards grants of $500 to $5,000, $145,000 in total. Projects must be rooted in the visual arts: interdisciplinary work in performance or other media qualifies only where visual art is clearly central, film is eligible during the creation phase but not for post-production or distribution, and sound art is generally eligible where the work sits within an expanded visual art context. Applications must be collaborative, with two to six collaborators and one named Primary Contact - the fund explicitly does not support the work of an individual artist working alone. The Primary Contact must live in the Portland, Oregon metropolitan area and in Oregon; collaborators may live anywhere. Every funded project must include a meaningful public component, may not be the core programming of a 501(c)(3), and may not be submitted through fiscal sponsorship. Grant funds can cover artist fees and collaborator compensation, exhibition production and installation, materials and fabrication, equipment rental, publication and printing, accessibility services, documentation, venue rental, administration, marketing and project-related transport. Applications typically include a project title and description, a project timeline, a statement of artistic intent, a description of public engagement, collaborator information, a project budget, work samples and any supporting materials. Viewing the pre-recorded Round 15 information session is required before applying, and optional 15-minute conversations with staff are offered afterwards. A panel of artists, curators, organisers, writers and other members of the visual arts community reviews all eligible applications through discussion rather than numerical scoring alone, and may award full or partial funding. Applications opened August 10 and close Sunday September 20, 2026 at 11:59pm PDT, with panel review in early November, notification in mid-November, the public announcement in early December and a grant period running January to December 2027. Free to apply, through Submittable. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500–$5,000.

item.title: 2027 Wedding Cake House Residencies · Dirt Palace
item.description: Dirt Palace, the artist-run space in Providence, Rhode Island, offers short, project-based residencies in the Wedding Cake House with a focus on mid-career artists, and is taking applications for the full suite of its 2027 offerings. Nine sessions are on the calendar, each running a week or a little longer: group residencies from January 12-21, January 28 - February 6 and November 14-22, where artists apply individually or in small groups and are placed in a cohort alongside other artists; a Family Teen residency February 14-20 for artist parents attending with children aged 13-16; a Caregiver group residency March 1-10 for artists who act as caregivers in their personal lives or professions; a Super Duo March 18-27 and Duo residencies April 6-15 and December 6-15 for pairs who apply together, with no requirement that they collaborate; and a Family Youth residency July 25 - August 1 for artists with children aged 8-12 (the info page's own section for that residency says 7-12; the season date list, the application question block and the apply page all say 8-12). There are no fees to apply or to attend and no stipends or travel budgets. Residents are housed; group residencies provide breakfast, lunch and groceries for dinner, with each resident cooking one dinner and helping to prep another, and duo residents get a welcome meal and kitchen access. Everyone also has access to facilities at Dirt Palace Classic, the organisation's original live/work space, including a print shop, a large workroom and a sound rehearsal studio. Days are unstructured, with residents asked to keep errands and outside work to a minimum; group residencies eat together each evening and hold an in-house artist talk, presentation, activity or reading by each resident afterwards, and close with a public component that often takes the form of an open house, open studio, talk, screening or performance. Work made on site has included writing and research, audio mixing and recording, video editing, photography, collage, drawing, sewing and durational performance art. The 2027 call is framed around the line 'No one's coming to save us', and the organisers are looking for artists whose starting point is figuring out how to keep making work that is responsive to this moment. Applications are no longer limited to artists living in New England, though preference goes to artists from New England and Rhode Island in particular; international applications are not accepted this year, and non-artists collaborating with artists may be part of a duo. Applications close October 15, 2026, with applicants notified the week of December 1. Free, through Submittable. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency.

item.title: The Art of Illustration · The Firefly Artists
item.description: The Firefly Artists, an artist cooperative founded in Northport, New York in 2011 and now running a gallery at 90 Main Street, asks for work that tells a story: book covers, movie posters, magazine spreads, comic pages, illustrated passages, political cartoons, articles or poems, with type incorporated or sent separately. Pieces are judged "not only on artistic merit but also how well it tells and sells the story". The framing is illustration-led - the gallery's own calendar heads it "Illustrator Show" - but photography is not a guest here: it is named in the accepted-media list on both the eligibility and the requirements pages ("drawing, painting, photography, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, collage, fabric work, glasswork, jewelry and digital media"), and the gallery's no-reproductions rule carries an explicit carve-out, "No reproductions will be accepted, with the exception of photography and digital art". Editorial, book-cover and photo-illustration work is squarely in scope. Entry is $35 for the first image and $5 for each of up to three more; artists nationwide may apply and there is no age bar. Awards are First Prize $150, Second Prize $75, Third Prize $50 and Honorable Mention, and nothing in the awards block narrows the eligible pool by medium. Work must be original and human-made - AI-generated art is not eligible, nor is anything made under close instruction in a workshop or class. Maximum frame size is 36 inches on the longest side, sculpture no larger than 12 inches in any direction; accepted work must arrive framed, wired and ready to hang, with plexiglass rather than glass on anything 16x20 inches or larger. All work must be for sale and the gallery takes a 35% commission; artists insure their own work while it is on view. Acceptance letters go out 22 October, selected work drops off 1, 4 and 5 November, the show hangs from Saturday 7 November to Sunday 6 December 2026 in the gallery's Darcy Arts Center exhibition space with a reception on Thursday 12 November, and pickup runs 7, 9 and 12 December - after which the gallery charges $5 a day in storage, and work still unclaimed 90 days after the show closes becomes the property of the gallery. — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: $35 (first image) + $5 each additional, up to 4. Prize: $150 + $75 + $50.

item.title: Artist-in-Residence — July–November 2027 · Surel's Place
item.description: Surel's Place runs month-long live-work residencies in Garden City, Idaho, in the late artist Surel Mitchell's own home and studio, and it takes applications against two fixed deadlines a year. This is the second of them: 1 March 2027, for residencies beginning roughly four months later. There is no application fee and no residency fee - rent, utilities and wi-fi are covered, and residents receive a living stipend of $100 a week, a $300 travel stipend, the use of the house bicycles, free or discounted tickets to local art events, marketing through the organisation's channels, and logistics and installation help for their public events. Each resident is assigned a host who introduces them to the local arts community, and one residency each cycle includes outreach to local schools through the PARTNER Schools Program. Photography is not in the org's medium list - it names "painters, writers, musicians, architects, filmmakers, and choreographers" - but the governing clause is "any artist who needs a place to focus", and the organisation's own upcoming-artists roster currently lists Eli Craven, October 2026, Photography/Sculpture. The property cannot take loud or messy processes such as welding or blacksmithing, and the org warns that work which is predominantly conceptual may find less enthusiasm with the jury. Residents must live at the house, take no other employment during the stay, give at least one public workshop of two to three hours, present a show or lecture on the residency work, and donate one piece to Surel's Place for future fundraising; the commission on sales arising from a residency is 35% of the retail price, dropping to 15% on merchandise or on work tangential to your medium, such as books. Applicants must be 25 or older and genuine non-smokers - the whole property is non-smoking and the org is blunt about it. Partners may join - no more than two adults, and there may be a surcharge for the extra utilities - but children and pets cannot. Note that the March round is when applications from playwrights and screenwriters reopen after a pause. One thing to confirm with the org before you plan travel: the apply page's deadline table gives this round's window as July to November 2027, while the FAQ and the apply page's own note about literary applicants both say July to December. Visual artists complete the online Artist-in-Residence Application in one sitting - it cannot be saved part-way - and email the accompanying cover letter, proposal including a workshop outline, CV, and 4 to 6 images with an image list by midnight MST on the deadline; the organisation says late applications can be held for the next round. — Deadline: March 1, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: 1-month residency + stipends.

item.title: Seeing Sound · New Orleans Photo Alliance
item.description: The New Orleans Photo Alliance - the 501(c)(3) behind the annual PhotoNOLA festival, now in its 21st year, and a gallery on Magazine Street - joins the New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Foundation for a show about the long relationship between music and photography: from stages to streets, from full orchestras to solo practice sessions. Entrants are asked to think broadly about form, format, process and approach, and the call is pitched in the spirit of Roy DeCarava's The Sound That I Saw, inviting a wide and improvisational approach to lens-based work about the sound and images that move us, in New Orleans and beyond. The juror is Bruce “Sunpie” Barnes, a New Orleans musician, photographer, author and former National Park Service ranger of thirty years who has played his own Afro-Louisiana music - blues, zydeco, gospel, Caribbean and African influenced rhythms - in more than fifty countries. Submissions are open to all photographers, NOPA membership is not required and all ages are accepted. Fine-art nudes and implied nudes are acceptable and digitally manipulated work is welcome; AI-generated photographs are not permitted. One wrinkle in the prospectus: the written instructions cap entries at five pieces while the CaFE upload form is configured for three to ten images, and the lower written figure is what is stored here. Entry is $35, or $25 for NOPA members, with bundles at $60 (fee plus a new basic membership) and $85 (fee plus a Silver membership including an online portfolio listing). Selected work is dropped off at the NOPA Center, 2011 Magazine Street, or shipped with a return label to NOPA's mailbox service at 3436 Magazine Street #134 - the prospectus warns that packages are not guaranteed at the gallery address; the show opens in late October 2026 and stays up through December and PhotoNOLA Fest. Sales are split 60/40 in the artist's favour and photographers pay shipping. NOPA's own open-calls page still lists earlier 2026 calls, so the organiser-authored CaFE prospectus is currently the only live surface for this edition. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $35 ($25 NOPA members; $60 or $85 bundled with a new membership). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: CURRENTS 2026 · New Orleans Photo Alliance
item.description: CURRENTS is the annual PhotoNOLA showcase at the Ogden Museum of Southern Art, and the one exhibition the New Orleans Photo Alliance reserves for its own members: eight to ten portfolios chosen to give an overview of contemporary photographic practices and projects, with up to four images hung per selected photographer. Membership is the only gate and it can be bought at the point of entry, with the NOPA team verifying membership before jurying begins. Watch the fee, though: the prospectus text promises members a $25 submission fee and a $60 entry-plus-membership bundle, but the CaFE entry form itself prints a single $35 entry fee with no member rate, and offers membership only as a separate $35 basic or $60 Silver charge - so joining at entry works out at $70 rather than $60. NOPA's other current call on the same portal does show a discounted member row, so the missing discount here looks like a configuration slip worth querying before you pay. The 2026 juror is Bill Boling, a book publisher and the creator of Fall Line Press, who lives and works in Milledgeville, Georgia; he studied photography under Stephen Shore at Bard in the early 2000s and has exhibited at the New Museum in New York and the Window Gallery at the University of Auckland. Entrants submit between four and ten images, JPG, up to 5MB, sized to 1800 pixels on the short side. Photographers accepted into the immediately preceding CURRENTS are asked to sit this one out, and images shown in previous CURRENTS exhibitions cannot be resubmitted - though different images from a previously featured series are eligible. Selected work must arrive framed and ready to hang at the NOPA Center rather than the Ogden, and shipping is the artist's responsibility. The exhibition runs 4 December 2026 to 1 February 2027 during the 21st PhotoNOLA festival. PhotoNOLA's own calls-for-entries page still lists the 2025 edition, so the organiser-authored CaFE prospectus is the live surface for this cycle. — Deadline: October 16, 2026. Fee: $35 (prospectus text promises members $25; the entry form lists no member rate) + $35 or $60 to join at entry. Prize: Exhibition at the Ogden Museum of Southern Art.

item.title: Joshua Tree Highlands Artist Residency 2027–2028
item.description: JTHAR is an artist-centric nonprofit residency established in 2007 that each year invites six artists from around the world to work in the high desert near the west entrance of Joshua Tree National Park. Three seven-week residencies are on offer for 2027-2028: 4 May to 22 June 2027, 24 August to 12 October 2027, and 11 January to 29 February 2028 - though jthar.org's own summary labels that third window January to March 2028, a month wider than the prospectus, so confirm the winter dates if that is the session you want. Each resident is assigned their own house on five acres of panoramic desert, may work there or in the JTHAR studio - a large space divided by movable walls - and receives a $1,500 scholarship to defray the cost of taking part, spendable on materials, transport or meals. Photography is named outright in the accepted media alongside drawing, painting, sculpture, film, video, new media, installation, fiction and non-fiction writing, interdisciplinary work, social practice and architecture; musical submissions are not being accepted this cycle. Selection is by JTHAR board members and selected jurors on the merit of the portfolio and the residency proposal, with priority to proposals that anticipate transformations and discoveries inspired by place. Visual artists submit a minimum of five images and every applicant submits a project proposal. Three terms worth knowing before applying: residents are required to donate one completed work to the JTHAR program, artists must provide their own transport and need a vehicle for the stay, and the residency cannot accommodate partners, family members or pets - the seven weeks are attended in full, no exceptions. There is a mid-residency review with the board and the option of an open-studio exhibition at the end. Open to US and international artists aged 18 and over; the fee is non-refundable and JTHAR says it cannot waive it, as it funds the residency stipends. Applications open on 15 September 2026 and close 15 December 2026 at 11:59 PM Mountain Time, with selected artists announced on 28 February 2027. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: $1,500 scholarship + seven-week residency.

item.title: Art Squared 2026 · Metro Art Studios
item.description: Metro Art Studios is a 501(c)(3) housed in a three-storey renovated corset factory in Bridgeport's South End, with 38 loft studios for professional musicians and visual artists and Crown Gallery on the ground floor. Art Squared is its annual fundraising exhibit, timed to open during the city-wide Bridgeport Art Trail, which brings close to 2,000 visitors through the building over the weekend. Every work is square - a minimum of 10 x 10 inches and a maximum of 14 x 14 inches including any frame - and is priced by the artist at $100, $200 or $300, with a 50% commission retained by Metro and 50% paid to the artist within 30 days of the show closing. All wall-hung fine art media are welcome and photography is named explicitly, alongside painting, printmaking, textiles and mixed media; work must be finished and able to hang on a single nail. There is no entry fee and each artist may submit up to three original works, one image per work. Entries must be entirely the entrant's own and made without an instructor's supervision; copies of existing artworks or work based on others' copyrighted art are not eligible. Open to artists aged 18 and over: the prospectus's eligibility section sets no geographic bar while its summary describes the show as an opportunity for artists of the greater Bridgeport region, and the binding practical constraint is that accepted work must be dropped off in person at Metro Art Studios on 21 October, 1 to 3 pm - the prospectus calls that a Saturday, but 21 October 2026 falls on a Wednesday, so confirm the day with the gallery before you plan the trip.
